title: Register your dog or cat in NSW
summary: Learn how to register your dog or cat for life on the NSW Pet Registry.
intro:
All pet dogs and cats in NSW need to be registered on the NSW Pet Registry. This must be done after the animal has been microchipped, and:

Registration covers the dog or cat for its lifetime, even if their owner changes.
who_can_apply: You must be aged 18 or over to own a dog or cat.
The pet must be microchipped prior to being registered.
what_you_need: If unable to register online, you may need documentation regarding the pet's transfer or origin (interstate/overseas).

how_to_steps.text: Select 'Log in to NSW Pet Registry'.
Log in or create your MyServiceNSW Account.
Follow the prompts to create your Pet Registry profile.
Select 'Register a pet' on your dashboard.
Follow the prompts to pay the registration fee.
Visit your local council, with your documentation and registration fee (if applicable).

more_info.text: additional fee if you do not desex your dog by 6 months of age
annual permit fee if you do not desex your cat by 4 months of age.
Your pet does not have to be desexed at the time of registration. In NSW, there are additional charges for owning a non-desexed pet.

faqs.q: Does pet registration cover the pet for life?
faqs.a: Yes, registration covers the dog or cat for its lifetime, even if the owner changes.

faqs.q: What is required before I can register my pet?
faqs.a: The pet must be microchipped before registration.

faqs.q: Who is responsible for microchipping the pet?
faqs.a: The person who is selling or giving the pet away is responsible for having the animal microchipped.
